key_claims: Syria is now run by a US-designated terrorist whose former group HTS, still an FTO, forms the bulk of his government, yet the US lifted sanctions after a 33-minute Trump–al-Sharaa meeting brokered by Saudi Arabia and Turkey.
Reuters traced the March 2025 massacre of ~1,500 Alawites to the top of the al-Sharaa government; the government 'got a pass' for March with snap-back sanctions only for future abuses.

A Syria–Israel peace treaty is not viable: no Israeli PM can cede the Golan after Oct 7, and al-Sharaa cannot survive conceding it given Syrian public opinion, his jihadist coalition, Turkey, and his own Golan family roots.
Expect a limited security arrangement instead, e.g. coordination against Palestinian/Iranian-backed factions in southern Syria, as recent unopposed IDF raids near Damascus suggest.
Even limited cooperation with Israel will face pushback from al-Sharaa's jihadist allies raised on bin Laden's 1998 fatwa; how he handles that will define his presidency.

Intelligence on the Iran strikes is politicised on both sides in the US; Israel's assessment is broadly that the strikes succeeded; Roggio recalls the 50-100 al-Qaeda-in-Afghanistan estimate as a precedent for manipulated intel.
